image: Editorial still-life photograph, extreme close-up of a single Iceland poppy (Papaver nudicaule) in vivid tangerine orange. Four large crinkled tissue-paper petals forming a shallow cup, translucent where the light passes through, fine creases still visible from being folded in the bud. A ribbed pale-green stigma disc with radiating rays, ringed by a dense crown of golden-yellow stamens. A slender hairy green stem curving down out of the bottom of the frame. The flower sits right of centre and fills about half the frame, leaving calm empty space on the left. Soft diffused daylight from the upper left, crisp focus on the stamens, shallow depth of field, modern fashion-magazine aesthetic, true-to-life colour, ultra detailed. Seamless, perfectly flat pale warm-grey studio backdrop (#E8E6E1) filling every edge of the frame, evenly lit, no gradient, no vignette, no shadow or reflection on the backdrop, nothing else in the scene.
video: Locked-off macro time-lapse, the camera does not move at all. One continuous take of the poppy's whole cycle: first the open flower slowly folds its crinkled tangerine petals inward, closing tighter and tighter until it has become a plump hairy green bud again, nodding gently on its stem. After a brief pause the bud lifts its head, its sepals split, and the crumpled petals unfold and smooth out into a wide open cup once more, revealing the golden stamens and the green stigma disc. Then a soft, slow breeze: the petals flutter and ripple at their edges and the flower sways a few millimetres on its stem. Smooth, graceful, dreamy motion. The stem stays rooted in the same place and the flower returns to the same place and size. The flat pale grey backdrop stays perfectly uniform and still. No new objects, no cuts.
